submission.natural_language_explanation: N2147+ is the open half of a single rectified linear read, not a clean category detector: this SwiGLU unit's gate is closed (g<0) on ~98% of tokens, so the activation equals silu(g)*u, is non-zero only where the layer-13 post-attention hidden state's up-projection u is negative, and has size |silu(g)|*|u| (r=0.96 with |u|), i.e. a weak broad dial (median 0.01, mean 0.05 over 14k tokens of ordinary web text, no dependence on token frequency, surprisal, next-token entropy, position or word length, all |r|<0.06). Its text-level bias is a rise to 0.15-0.38 on quantitative/comparative wording (more than half of, at least, almost, about) and on nouns naming abstract, institutional or technical kinds after a definite determiner (registry, database, market, journal, protocol, pipeline, treaty, enzyme, cell, population, size), while animate or everyday-individual referents (bakery, kitchen, rabbit, puppy, bicycle), demonstratives (this/these/those) and clause punctuation sit at 0.00-0.06; the split is partial, since some institutional words (committee, budget, revenue) also sit near zero.

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
Memo: Quarterly Review of the Regional Water Monitoring Programme

To: All programme leads
From: Office of the Director
Date: 14 March

This memo summarises progress on the monitoring programme and sets out the items that require attention before the next funding cycle.

Background. The programme was established to track water quality across eleven river catchments. Field teams collect samples at fixed stations and upload readings to a central archive. Equipment was replaced in stages, and the last batch arrived in February. Staffing has been stable, though two technicians rotated onto night shifts.

Progress this quarter. Field teams completed 412 scheduled visits. Coverage held steady in the northern catchments; the southern stations lagged because access roads were flooded for a week. The maintenance team repaired four sensors and recalibrated the rest. Training sessions ran in January and again in March, with attendance recorded for each session.

Issues. Two stations reported intermittent connectivity. The vendor traced the fault to a firmware update pushed in December. A workaround is in place, and the vendor expects a permanent patch before the end of the quarter. Separately, the archive team noticed gaps in the record where uploads failed silently; the missing entries were reconstructed from field notebooks and the log is now complete.

Financial position. Expenditure tracked close to plan. Travel costs ran higher than budgeted because of the flooded roads, and equipment costs came in lower. The finance office will revise the forecast before the next cycle.

Actions required. Programme leads should confirm staffing for the summer rotation by the end of the month. Station managers should submit maintenance logs through the registry rather than by email, so that the database stays current. The protocol for sensor calibration was updated last year and must be followed exactly, including the two-step verification. Any deviation requires written approval. The review panel will meet in April and will look at the pipeline from sampling to publication, since delays there have been the main source of slippage. A short summary will appear in the quarterly journal, and the panel will report at least twice a year to the funders.

Risks. The main risk is staff turnover. A second risk is dependence on a single vendor for sensors. Management is exploring alternatives, though a switch would take months. A third risk is that the population of trained technicians in the region is small, and competing employers recruit actively.

Recommendation. Continue the programme as planned, address the firmware fault, migrate uploads to the registry, and report progress in the quarterly journal. The next review is scheduled for June.
